name: City Palace
story: Begun by Maharana Udai Singh II in 1553 and extended by successive Mewar rulers, the City Palace is a cluster of palaces, courtyards and balconies stacked along the east bank of Lake Pichola. Its mix of Rajput and Mughal motifs is visible in the mirror-work Mor Chowk and the lake-facing zenana balconies.

name: Jag Mandir
story: Jag Mandir, the 'Lake Garden Palace', sits on an island in Lake Pichola. Built across the 17th century, it sheltered Prince Khurram — later Shah Jahan — during his exile, and its gul mahal is often linked to the inspiration behind later Mughal architecture.

name: Bagore Ki Haveli
story: An 18th-century haveli on Gangaur Ghat with over a hundred rooms, glass-and-mirror inlay and a museum of Mewari costume, turbans and puppetry. Evenings host a traditional folk-dance performance.

name: Jagdish Temple Lanes
story: Built in 1651, the Indo-Aryan Jagdish Temple anchors a web of narrow lanes where miniature painters, silversmiths and textile printers still work from small ground-floor studios.

name: Saheliyon Ki Bari
story: A 18th-century garden of fountains, lotus pools and marble kiosks, created for the women of the royal court — a calmer alternative to the palace crowds, close to Fateh Sagar.
